title: Herdr-lab course manifest (herdr-lab/course.v1)
description: Validates the parsed course.yaml manifest. The YAML on disk is the human-edited source of truth; course-vet.py parses it with PyYAML and validates against this schema. A manifest is the contract between a course author and herdr-lab §6/§7: it declares the canonical lesson layout, the module grouping, the student shell (so snippets adapt - fish $status vs bash $?), the scratch bootstrap, and the quiz passing score. Markdown stays the spine (see SKILL.md s6 Course-content-intake); this manifest only makes the spine navigable and machine-checkable.

schema.description: Format version. herdr-lab treats unknown values as 'unsupported' and tells the agent, rather than guessing.

name.description: Course slug, lowercase kebab (e.g. 'algal-wgs'). Used for pane/tab labels and score files.

title.description: Human-readable course title for chat summaries.

shell.description: The shell in which lesson exercises are expected to run. §6 uses this to flag snippet crossovers (fish: $status vs $?, 'set VAR val' vs export) before dictating a command.

scratch_setup.description: Path (relative to the course root) of a script that bootstraps the pane's scratch cwd before lesson 01 (downloads fixtures, seeds directories). §6 runs it once via herdr_pane run at pane setup if present; the agent narrates every line it runs.

passing_score.description: Fraction of quiz points required for the §7 closing summary to declare a pass. Points come from items[].points; unweighted items count 1.

modules.description: Ordered modules; lesson order inside a module is the teaching order across the whole course (depth-first).

id.description: Module slug (e.g. 'phase-1'). Referenced by lesson frontmatter 'module'.

lessons.description: Lesson directory slugs, in teaching order. Each must contain README.md and match a lessons/ directory sibling-of-manifest.
